meta.title: Real tmux in the browser — prefix key, panes, truecolor
meta.description: A tmux browser client: a real prefix key, a mobile keyboard row, pane reflow for small screens, truecolor rendering and reconnects that keep the session.

hero.title: Everything a terminal needs. Nothing a phone can't do.
hero.lead: mtmux is a faithful tmux client that happens to run in a browser tab. The hard parts are input, layout and getting there at all — so that is where the work went.

input.title: The modifier row
input.prose: Mobile keyboards hide the keys terminals live on. mtmux puts them back: a persistent row with the prefix key, esc, ctrl, alt, tab and the arrows. Modifiers latch, so ⌃b % is two taps rather than a contortion.
bullets: The prefix key is a real key, not a menu item
Modifiers latch, so chords are taps rather than holds
A hardware Bluetooth keyboard passes chords straight through
Signal buttons for the interrupts you actually send
input.diagramAlt: The on-screen modifier row: a prefix key, esc, ctrl, alt, tab and arrow keys, plus a row of interrupt shortcuts.

layout.title: Reflow, not squinting
layout.prose: A three-column layout on a 34-inch monitor is unusable at 390px. Reflow restacks panes vertically, keeps the focused pane full width, and never resizes the underlying tmux window — so your desktop layout is exactly where you left it.
bullets: Per-device client size, independent of the server window
Tap a pane to focus it, and the rest get out of the way
A session and window switcher built for a thumb
On a tablet, real splits with room to actually use them
layout.diagramAlt: A three-pane desktop layout reflows into a stacked single column with the focused pane full-width on a phone.

rest.title: Details that decide whether you keep it

cells.title: Truecolor and glyphs
cells.body: 24-bit colour, powerline separators, box drawing and Nerd Font icons, rendered on a WebGL canvas.

cells.title: Copy-mode that copies
cells.body: Select in copy-mode and the selection lands in the device clipboard as well as the tmux buffer.

cells.title: Scrollback search
cells.body: Search a pane's history and jump between matches, with the same keys you already use.

cells.title: Reconnects on its own
cells.body: A dropped WebSocket reconnects and reattaches without you doing anything. Cellular handoffs are survivable.

cells.title: Sessions, windows and panes
cells.body: Create, rename, switch and kill from the UI — <post>the operations you would otherwise reach for the prefix key to do</post>.

cells.title: A file browser
cells.body: Read a diff or a log in the same tab. Paths are allow-listed, so a paired browser only reaches what you allow.

cells.title: Themes and type
cells.body: Terminal theme, font size and cursor style are per-device and persisted, because a phone wants different values than a desktop.

cells.title: No account required
cells.body: Signing in is optional and only buys more registered servers. The tunnel and local mode work without one.

cells.title: Honest offline behaviour
cells.body: When the connection is gone, the UI says so instead of showing you a frozen screen you might mistake for a live one.
